debate.text: Fenmoor has a £310,000 gap on two country buses once the fare is capped at £2. Every answer broke a promise: a tax rise, a £3 fare, or four villages with no weekday bus. I signed nothing. The jury says rethink the tax promise, 8 to 4. I will not strand a village on the 14. It is their only bus.

Joe, I did the sum. £310,000 across the town's homes is about £14 a year each. That is less than a pint a month. Elderbrook's winter fund cost more per head and nobody sent that back. The citizens may have set the tax red line without seeing the figure.

A rural worker with no weekday bus loses the job, not just the ride. Dunmarrow's late minibus paid for itself in that sense. But £14 on a pay packet is real for a household already on the edge. Mira's pint is somebody else's tea.

Both fair. I will not tell the town to drop the tax promise. I will tell them what it costs a house and what it costs a village, and let them choose. A bus for every village comes before a bus for every pound.
